comparator.name: Bachelor Bedrijfskunde
comparator.sourceNotes: The July 2026 curriculum defines a 180-EC bachelor with a 60-EC first year, 60-EC second year and a 60-EC third year. For year 3, this pathway preserves 30 EC of genuine choice space as a 15-EC minor plus 15 EC of unnamed electives, then includes the compulsory Advanced Research Skills, Methods Master Classes and Cross Cultural Management and instantiates the Entrepreneurship for Growth track (17 EC). Entrepreneurship is selected under the neutral broad-identity rule because the programme explicitly makes entrepreneurship central across the first two years; the choice is not based on UCR fit.

alternatives.label: Business, management & entrepreneurship
alternatives.concept: A broad business-administration route combining entrepreneurship and strategy with accounting, finance, economics, marketing, leadership, organisational behaviour, research, data and international business.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is broader than a single business subfield, combining management and entrepreneurship with economics, finance, marketing, research, data and global business.
progression: Business, economics, data and research foundations precede advanced strategy, law, leadership, econometrics and market research; all formal prerequisites occur earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Business, sustainability & responsible management
alternatives.concept: A business route organised around sustainable business strategy, circular operations, responsible leadership and sustainable marketing while retaining core management, economics, research and legal foundations.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines a substantial sustainability sequence with business strategy, marketing, leadership, economics, research and law, so the label names both business and sustainability rather than implying a pure sustainability programme.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces much of the general economics, data, communication and technology mix with a sequenced sustainability curriculum focused on climate, circularity, governance, renewable systems and sustainable operations.
progression: Sustainability Essentials I precedes Sustainability Essentials II, which precedes advanced circular-resource and renewable-system work; business and research foundations precede advanced law, public economics, leadership and market research, with all formal prerequisites completed earlier.

alternatives.label: Finance, analytics & business decision-making
alternatives.concept: A finance and analytics route combining accounting, finance and economics with econometrics, probability, data science, machine learning, programming and optimisation for business decision-making.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is organised around finance and quantitative analysis but still contains strategy, international business and negotiation, so the label explicitly combines finance, analytics and business decision-making.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match and the sustainability route, this curriculum substitutes mathematics, programming, databases, optimisation, probability and additional economics/finance for much of the leadership, marketing, communication and sustainability content.
progression: Programming and mathematical methods precede decision algorithms, linear algebra and probability; economics and research foundations precede advanced economics, econometrics, finance and market research, with all formal prerequisites completed earlier and all courses offered in their assigned terms.

routeSelection.basis: The generic Bedrijfskunde programme has three formal third-year tracks. Entrepreneurship is explicitly central across the first two years, including venture creation, innovation and growth, so Entrepreneurship for Growth most directly continues the programme-wide academic identity. The choice is independent of UCR fit.

selection.assessment: Two additional generator-backed directions are coherent and feasible after the closest match: Sustainable Business Strategies and Financial Analysis & Investment. Both produce curricula that are substantively distinct and exceed the 30-EC pairwise floor, so the maximum of three UCR alternatives is reached.

blocks: Market Research provides applied research design, data collection and analysis for a business problem.
Econometrics directly covers regression-based quantitative analysis central to the comparator methods master classes.
Database Management Systems provides a specific information-management foundation through organisational data structures and SQL.
Both examine how cultural and institutional environments shape management and international business decisions.

notes.text: RSM Bedrijfskunde provides a dense compulsory sequence across business functions, including primary processes, HRM, supply-chain management, management accounting and simulation, plus a formal third-year track and bachelor project. UCR can build coherent business, sustainability and finance/analytics programmes, but it does not reproduce the same complete functional sequence or formal track/project structure.
